dedupe_keys.name: resie simulation engine for district scale sector coupled energy systems quasi

description: ReSiE is an open-source simulation engine for district-scale, sector-coupled energy systems that link heat, electricity and other carriers, developed within the QuaSi project by Etienne Ott, Heiner Steinacker, Maksim Helmann, Adrian Vollmer and Elias Demartin. It simulates power, heat and other energy flows between components such as heat pumps, CHP units, batteries, electrolysers and ground-coupled heat storage, with economic, emissions and black-box optimisation options, driven by an interactive command-line interface that keeps compiled code between runs for faster repeated simulations. The method is location-independent. It is written in Julia (version 1.10 or later, tested to 1.12.2) and registered as the Julia package ResieQuasi, with documentation on Read the Docs, releases archived on Zenodo, and version 1.0.2 (September 2026) as the latest release. It is released under the MIT licence at no cost, with some external files under their own licences. Caveats: the Julia package name differs from the project name, and users need Julia installed. Simulation uses are planning and operational analysis of district heating and sector-coupled neighbourhood energy systems. Related records: none linked on the provider's pages read on the day.
